body.statement: Can a local-action lower bound show \(n^{3/2}\mathcal E_n(m)\to\infty\) when \(m\to\infty\) but \(m=o(\sqrt n)\)?  The handle is the LAN-to-action bridge with the empirical information limit and exact finite-boundary localization made explicit.
body.justification: This is the vanishing-pilot endpoint of the proposed square-root balance.
body.gap: Its expected divergence is only heuristic until the LAN and exact finite-action bridges are proved.
body.consumer: It supplies the lower-end coercivity premise in the conditional global theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: The local-action lower bound when the pilot diverges more slowly than \(\sqrt n\).
obligation.obstruction: The candidate \(1/(nm)\) regret rate requires both an information limit and the exact finite-action curvature bridge, neither of which follows from the frozen primitives.
obligation.attempted: Computed the candidate Gaussian quadratic constant and isolated the missing empirical-information convergence with an explicit counterexample.
obligation.partial_result: The candidate Gaussian-shift regret is of order \(1/(nm)\), which would diverge after multiplication by \(n^{3/2}\) when \(m=o(\sqrt n)\).  The empirical-information limit and exact finite-action transfer needed to make that calculation valid are not implied by the current assumptions.
